title: Fruitvale Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Fruitvale wells are typically 20 feet deep, but yields are often low. See local drilling costs, water levels, risks, and permit history.
h1: Fruitvale, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost
intro_html:
Well records around Fruitvale show a shallow but highly variable groundwater setting. The median constructed depth is 20 feet, and the middle half of reported wells falls between 15 and 29 feet. That does not mean every lot will have an easy well. The record includes a deepest well of 4,629 feet, while most wells are completed in unnamed or fractured-bedrock conditions.

Yield data is limited, with only 27 wells reporting a pump yield. The available results still matter: the median is 0.1 gallons per minute, and 63% report less than 1 gallon per minute. A buyer near Clifton, Orchard Mesa, or Grand Junction should verify the neighboring well pattern before relying on a map average.

sections.heading: Fruitvale well depths are usually shallow, with important exceptions
sections.html:
Among the 672 wells reporting total depth, the median is 20 feet. The middle half runs from 15 to 29 feet, and the 90th percentile is 35 feet. That pattern points to shallow groundwater or shallow completion practices across much of Fruitvale.

The depth mix is unusually concentrated: 96% are under 100 feet, while 2% fall between 100 and 300 feet, 1% between 300 and 600 feet, and 1% exceed 600 feet. A driller's bid should still allow for local changes in alluvial material, sedimentary rock, or fractured bedrock. Nearby properties in Clifton and Orchard Mesa may not predict a specific lot.

sections.heading: Fruitvale well yields call for conservative water planning
sections.html:
Only 27 permits report a pump yield, so the yield statistics are a limited sample rather than a guarantee. The median reported yield is 0.1 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 0.1 to 5.0 gallons per minute. Most importantly for a buyer, 63% of reported wells produce under 1 gallon per minute.

The remaining records are split between stronger results: 15% report 5 to 15 gallons per minute, and 22% report more than 15 gallons per minute. That spread is why storage capacity, pump testing, and intended household demand matter. Do not assume a shallow well will provide irrigation water simply because a nearby well does.

sections.heading: Water levels in Fruitvale are deeper in newer records
sections.html:
The reported median static water level is 18 feet below ground surface, with the middle half between 10 and 22 feet. That is the depth to water when the well is not being pumped, not the total well depth and not the amount of water the well can produce.

The decade pattern deserves attention. Median static water levels were 9 feet in measurements from the 2000s, 10 feet in the 2010s, and 18 feet in the 2020s. That indicates deeper measured water levels in the newer records, although only 60 wells report static water levels and measurement conditions vary. Treat it as a local warning to check current neighboring wells, not as proof of a uniform decline.

sections.heading: Fruitvale permit history shows heavy monitoring activity
sections.html:
The records cover 1,208 permitted wells within 5 miles of Fruitvale, but the use mix is not dominated by household wells. Monitoring accounts for 80% of the permits, while domestic or household use accounts for 3% and irrigation for 1%. Stock use is recorded at 0%.

Permitting increased from 2 permits in the 1950s and 1 in the 1960s to 333 in the 2000s and 337 in the 2010s. There were 145 in the 2020s, with the newest permit year listed as 2025. The most active record name is Authorized, with 522 wells; Da Smith Drilling Company has 11.

sections.heading: What a Fruitvale well may cost to drill and finish
sections.html:
The local cost model uses mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground at roughly $50 to $75 per foot. At the 20-foot median depth, the drilled hole alone models at about $1,000 to $1,500. That is an excavation and drilling allowance, not a complete water system.

A finished well including the pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at about $7,000 to $13,500. The unusually deep outliers show why a written proposal should explain what happens if the driller must go beyond the expected shallow interval. Ask what casing, grout, pump testing, water-quality work, and difficult access are included before comparing bids.

sections.heading: Fruitvale buyers should investigate water quality, yield, and septic layout
sections.html:
Environmental screening is important here. Within about 10 miles are 66 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 19 historic mine features, and 37 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. These mapped sites do not prove that a particular well is contaminated, but they are good reasons to test the water and review the well's location and construction history.

Most permits name an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer, with 1,132 wells in that category, compared with 44 alluvial wells and 1 Mancos well. Fractured rock can be unpredictable, and a dry hole or low-yield result is possible. Confirm setbacks between the well, septic system, replacement area, buildings, and driveways before finalizing a site plan.

sections.heading: A practical Fruitvale plan for buying or building
sections.html:
Before closing on a rural property, obtain the DWR permit, construction report, pump information, and recent water test for the actual well. Compare it with nearby records in Fruitvale, Clifton, Grand Junction, and Orchard Mesa, paying close attention to reported yield and static water level rather than depth alone.

For a vacant lot, have a Colorado water professional review the intended use, legal water supply, access for a drill rig, septic feasibility, and electrical route before you commit to construction. A domestic or household well permit is not the same as an unlimited supply. If the basin is over-appropriated, an augmentation plan may be needed for some uses. Plan around storage when the well yield is low.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Fruitvale, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth near Fruitvale is 20 feet, and the middle half runs from 15 to 29 feet. Ninety-six percent of reported wells are under 100 feet. The records also include much deeper exceptions, including a deepest well of 4,629 feet, so a neighboring shallow well does not guarantee the same result on your lot.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Fruitvale?
faq.a: The local model uses $50 to $75 per foot. At Fruitvale's 20-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $1,000 to $1,500. A completed system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $7,000 to $13,500. Difficult ground, access, testing, and work beyond the expected depth can change the final bid.

faq.q: How much water do Fruitvale wells produce?
faq.a: Reported yields are highly variable, and only 27 wells list a pump yield. The median is 0.1 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 0.1 to 5.0 gallons per minute. Sixty-three percent report under 1 gallon per minute, while 22% report more than 15 gallons per minute. A pump test is important before relying on a well.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Fruitvale?
faq.a: The permit map cannot establish that a specific well is safe to drink. Within about 10 miles are 66 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 19 historic mine features, and 37 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Have the actual well tested, especially for contaminants relevant to nearby environmental sites, and review casing, grout, and septic separation.

faq.q: Are Fruitvale water levels getting lower?
faq.a: Reported median static water levels were 9 feet below ground in the 2000s, 10 feet in the 2010s, and 18 feet in the 2020s. That pattern shows deeper measurements in newer records, but only 60 wells report static water levels and conditions differ between measurements. Use the trend as a reason to check current neighboring wells, not as a guarantee of decline on every property.
